title: AssertionError in `ensure_vmecpp_input` when running VMEC++ with `simsopt_compat`
body:
#### Description
I encountered an `AssertionError` when trying to initialize a VMEC object using `simsopt_compat.Vmec()`. The error seems to occur in `ensure_vmecpp_input`, where the expected VMEC++ input path does not match the generated one.

#### **Steps to Reproduce**
1. Run:
   ```python
   import vmecpp
   vmec = vmecpp.simsopt_compat.Vmec("input.w7x")
   print(f"Computed plasma volume: {vmec.volume()}")
   ```
2. The following error occurs:

    ```python
      AssertionError                            Traceback (most recent call last)
      Cell In[10], line 1
      ----> 1 vmec = vmecpp.simsopt_compat.Vmec("input.w7x")
      
      File ~/.conda/envs/vmecpp/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vmecpp/simsopt_compat.py:133, in Vmec.__init__(self, filename, verbose, ntheta, nphi, range_surface, mpi, keep_all_files)
          130 # Original VMEC follows the convention that all input files start with `input`,
          131 # but VMEC++ does not (see e.g. the contents of vmecpp/test_data).
          132 if basename.startswith("input") or basename.endswith(".json"):
      --> 133     with ensure_vmecpp_input(Path(filename)) as vmecpp_filename:
          134         logger.debug(
          135             f"Initializing a VMEC object from input file: {vmecpp_filename}"
          136         )
          137         self.indata = vmec.VmecINDATAPyWrapper.from_file(vmecpp_filename)
      
      File ~/.conda/envs/vmecpp/lib/python3.12/contextlib.py:137, in _GeneratorContextManager.__enter__(self)
          135 del self.args, self.kwds, self.func
          136 try:
      --> 137     return next(self.gen)
          138 except StopIteration:
          139     raise RuntimeError("generator didn't yield") from None
      
      File ~/.conda/envs/vmecpp/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vmecpp/simsopt_compat.py:573, in ensure_vmecpp_input(input_path)
          568 output_file = input_path.with_name(f"{configuration_name}.{os.getpid()}.json")
          570 vmecpp_input_path = _util.indata_to_json(
          571     input_path, output_override=output_file
          572 )
      --> 573 assert vmecpp_input_path == output_file
          574 try:
          575     yield vmecpp_input_path
    ```

title: simsopt_compat cleanup
body: Currently we have `src/vmecpp/simsopt_compat.py` as well as `src/vmecpp/cpp/vmecpp/simsopt_compat/...`. I would like to suggest to migrate the Python sources outside of `src/vmecpp/cpp` and somehow merge then with what is in `src/vmecpp/simsopt_compat.py`.
author: jons-pf

comments.body:
I left this kind of clean-up for after we switch the monorepo to use these sources, because it otherwise makes it trickier to sync the sources here with those in the monorepo.

But if we never add anything new to the monorepo (not even those currently open PRs that add support for HINT-related quantities) we can start making large changes to the C++ sources already now.

title: Bazel build and cmake build may differ
body:
In particular bazel brings in some dependencies as bazel modules that the cmake build takes from the system. The version might be different.

Since Proxima uses bazel internally, means that we might end up seeing different behavior from cmake users, which might be confusing.

An alternative could be to fully switch to cmake and use the bazel-cmake adapter to build VMEC++ as part of a bazel build.
author: eguiraud-pf

comments.body: I think this has now been mostly resolved, as CMake pulls in (almost all) the dependencies from source with a pinned version. As long as the library versions are kept in sync, we should be good.

title: Build issues on macOS using non home-brew setups.
body:
There are a number of build issues when trying to compile in an environment that is not using home-brew.

### LAPACK ISSUES

The header and associated functions are not defined for the Accelerate framework.

lapacke.h
LAPACKE_dgetrs
LAPACKE_dgetrf

Recommend just forward declaring for fortran function interfaces directly for cross platform compatibility.

```
///  Compute double precision LU Factorization of a general mxn matrix.
extern "C" void dgetrf_(int *m,
                        int *n,
                        double *a,
                        int *lda,
                        int *ipiv,
                        int *info);
///  LU solve of a mxn matrix A.
extern "C" void dgetrs_(char *transpose,
                        int *num_rows,
                        int *num_columns,
                        double *matrix,
                        int *leading_dim,
                        int *pivot,
                        double *y,
                        int *y_leading_dim,
                        int *info);
```
Then calling these by
```
    int one = 1;
    int info;
    char transpose = 'N';
    dgetrs_(&transpose, &mnpd, &one, matrixShare.data(), &mnpd,
            iPiv.data(), bvecShare.data(), &mnpd, &info);
```
and 
```
  int info;
  dgetrf_(&mnpd, &mnpd, matrixShare.data(), &mnpd, iPiv.data(), &info);
```
after removing const from mnpd.

### BUILD ISSUES

Cmake build system is mis configured in a way that's causing an error.
```
make[2]: *** No rule to make target `/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX14.2.sdk/usr/lib/libm.tbd', needed by `vmec_standalone'.  Stop.
```


Hello Mark, thank you for your feedback! Unfortunately we only officially support homebrew on macos at this time, but we are very happy to accept patches that make it possible to use other installation methods too.

title: Some wout attributes are present in C++ but not exposed from the Python layer
body:
`VmecWOut._MISSING_FORTRAN_VARIABLES` reports all the variables that are not exposed by the Python API, but actually some of them are present in the C++ `WOutFileContents` and could easily be exposed, e.g. all the am/ac/ai quantities.

This was already implemented in Proxima's private version of VMEC++ but was not merged in time for the VMEC++ open-sourcing.

The latest state in Proxima's private version:

```
VARIABLES_MISSING_FROM_FORTRAN_WOUT_ADAPTER = [
    "input_extension",
    "itfsq",
    "fsqt",
    "wdot",
    "currumnc",
    "currvmnc",
    "curlabel",
    "potvac",
]
```

vs the open-source repo:

```
VARIABLES_MISSING_FROM_FORTRAN_WOUT_ADAPTER = [
    "input_extension",
    "nextcur",
    "extcur",
    "mgrid_mode",
    "am",
    "ac",
    "ai",
    "am_aux_s",
    "am_aux_f",
    "ai_aux_s",
    "ai_aux_f",
    "ac_aux_s",
    "ac_aux_f",
    "itfsq",
    "lrecon__logical__",
    "lrfp__logical__",
    "bdotb",
    "fsqt",
    "wdot",
    "currumnc",
    "currvmnc",
]
```

NOTE: we actually care about porting these to `VmecWOut`, not to `FortranWOutAdapter`.
